articles.title: Rio Ngumoha showing 'superstar' potential for Liverpool and making more dribbles than Jeremy Doku - The Radar
articles.summary: Rio Ngumoha's explosive performances for Liverpool are the focus of The Radar column; Luka Vuskovic's vital role for Brighton is also examined; watch Liverpool vs Brighton live on Sky Sports Premier League from 12.30pm on Sunday; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Ngumoha's stunning stats 🔺Vuskovic's key role for Brighton 🔺A player to watch this weekend

A seat in the Gtech Community Stadium press box last weekend offered a close-up view of Rio Ngumoha's game-changing talent. The 18-year-old played at a different speed to everyone else, a blur of stepovers and bewilderingly quick changes of direction.

Liverpool were trailing when he was sent on early in the second half for the injured Jeremie Frimpong but ended up claiming a vital win, inspired by the irrepressible skill and drive of a player whose final action was to draw the foul for Vitaly Janelt's red card.

Janelt had little hope of catching him fairly as he tore towards Brentford's box from inside his own half. Three days later, Villarreal couldn't even get close enough to foul him as he followed up his cameo in west London with an electrifying start at Anfield.

Aged 18 years and 52 days old, Ngumoha became the third-youngest player in Champions League history to provide two assists in a single game after Warren Zaire-Emery and Theo Walcott.

Villarreal doubled and even tripled up on him. It wasn't enough. First, he jinked inside and clipped a delicate, diagonal cross straight into the path of Ronald Araujo at the back post. Then, he danced to the byline and put the ball on a plate for Alexis Mac Allister.

Robbie Fowler, a former Liverpool prodigy himself, of course, called it a "statement performance" from the teenager. Daniel Sturridge raved about his "God-given ability". Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher labelled him a "future superstar".

His total of nine successful dribbles in the game took him to 18 in total in this season's Champions League, putting him six clear of Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, the next player on the list.

His one-on-one ability has been evident since his arrival on the scene last season, when he marked his Premier League debut with a stoppage-time winner against Newcastle before making a further 28 appearances in all competitions under Arne Slot.

His development has gathered pace under Andoni Iraola and his numbers have been similarly strong in the Premier League. Since the start of last term, his average of 4.47 successful dribbles per 90 minutes puts him ahead of even Manchester City's Jeremy Doku.

He is something of an outlier in terms of his efficiency.

Ngumoha's dribble success rate of 66 per cent since the start of last season puts him comfortably ahead of any of the other 150 players to have attempted at least 35 in the same timeframe.

Doku's success rate, to continue the comparison, is 52 per cent. The average among the same group of players is 42 per cent.

Ngumoha has played considerably fewer minutes than most of those players. His efficiency will be tested over a longer period.

But right now he looks unplayable. Across his last three appearances, he has completed a remarkable 19 out of 22 attempted dribbles.

It is all the more impressive given he has done it in a supposedly unfamiliar position. Ngumoha has played the majority of his minutes on the left since his Liverpool breakthrough but Iraola has moved him into the problematic right-wing role.

Liverpool are lighter on that side following Mohamed Salah's exit, with Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo better off the left. But Victor Munoz's injury may open the door for Ngumoha to make his first Premier League start of the season against Brighton on the right.

Carragher hopes it is just the start for him. "I hope he signs a new contract because right now, we've got a lot of wingers in the team, but he could be the best winger Liverpool have got," the Sky Sports pundit added after the Villarreal game.

"Liverpool have got a problem position on the right wing. We've got a lot of left wingers. Rio might be better on the left, but he was outstanding on the right tonight."

Iraola agreed, albeit while offering constructive criticism. "He struggled defensively in the first half," he said, before praising his attitude. "That's the good thing with Rio, he's still 18, he's not the full package and he can add things."

Iraola highlighted his left-footed shooting as one area of development and there has also been praise for his work in small pockets of space on the inside, where he offers vision and guile in addition to the outstanding dribbling ability shown on the outside.

Recent evidence suggests Brighton's toughest task at Anfield on Sunday might be finding a way to contain him.

One of the Brighton players tasked with stopping Ngumoha and Liverpool will be Luka Vuskovic . The 19-year-old centre-back, a club-record £50m signing from Spurs in July, has played an important role for Fabian Hurzeler's side at both ends of the pitch.

It is rare for a player of his age to be starting at centre-back in the Premier League but he has found his feet rapidly after spending last season on loan at Hamburg from Spurs. "What he has is the physicality to adapt quickly," said Hurzeler last month.

Those physical strengths can be seen in the numbers. Only two players have won more aerials or made more headed clearances. Vuskovic also ranks highly for duels won. His presence has helped Brighton keep four consecutive Premier League clean sheets.

The Seagulls have earned more plaudits for their attacking displays, though, having scored 23 goals in seven games, and Vuskovic has played his part on that front, too. Brighton's total includes eight goals from set-pieces. Vuskovic has added a new threat.

The Croatia scored a back-post header from a corner against Leeds in September. A similar effort against Crystal Palace last weekend allowed Jack Hinshelwood to score Brighton's fifth after it was parried back into the six-yard box by Walter Benitez.

Vuskovic's total of 13 shots is the most by any defender in the Premier League. It is a continuation of his efforts at Hamburg, where he racked up six Bundesliga goals in 28 appearances.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Bournemouth have started winning games and keeping clean sheets thanks in part to summer signing Antonio Silva . Manchester United, their opponent on Sunday, could use centre-back like him.

Five Premier League games are live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting with Chelsea vs Spurs on Saturday, kicking off at 5.30pm.

On Super Sunday , Crystal Palace vs Newcastle United , Hull City vs Brentford and Liverpool vs Brighton and Manchester United vs Bournemouth are all available to watch at 2pm. The action continues at 4.30pm, when Sunderland host Leeds United .

Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi was the focus of last week's column, then went and scored the winner against Newcastle. Brentford's Vitaly Janelt also featured. There was also a mention of some encouraging signs for Alvaro Arbeloa , who finally got a first Fulham win against Hull.

articles.title: Inglaterra manda, pero España aprieta: así está la batalla por el trono UEFA
articles.standfirst: La Premier sigue dominando el coeficiente UEFA de federaciones, pero LaLiga se mantiene al acecho gracias al rendimiento de sus clubes en Europa y a sus ocho representantes aún en competición
articles.summary: La Premier sigue dominando el coeficiente UEFA de federaciones, pero LaLiga se mantiene al acecho gracias al rendimiento de sus clubes en Europa y a sus ocho representantes aún en competición
articles.body: La jerarquía del fútbol europeo sigue hablando inglés, aunque España no pierde de vista la cabeza. Los últimos coeficientes UEFA sitúan a Inglaterra como la gran potencia continental con 119,519 puntos, por delante de Italia (99,946) y España (97,046), que se mantiene en la pelea gracias al excelente rendimiento colectivo de sus clubes en las últimas campañas. El dato cobra aún más relevancia al observar el presente curso. En la clasificación de coeficientes de la temporada, España aparece segunda con 22,093 puntos, únicamente superada por una intratable Inglaterra (28,680). Los clubes españoles siguen sumando con regularidad y aventajan a otras grandes ligas como la alemana (21,785), la portuguesa (20,500) y la italiana (19,000). Otro indicador que refleja la fortaleza del fútbol español es el número de representantes que continúan vivos en Europa. La federación española conserva ocho equipos en competición, una cifra que únicamente supera Inglaterra, con nueve. En cuanto al ranking de clubes, el dominio ya no pertenece al Real Madrid. El gigante blanco, habitual referencia europea, ocupa la segunda posición con 144,500 puntos, solo por detrás del Bayern de Múnich, líder con 147,500. Completa el podio el Paris Saint-Germain con 132,000 puntos. Si se analiza únicamente la última temporada, el protagonismo cambia de manos. El Arsenal lidera la clasificación anual con 44 puntos, seguido por el Bayern (39,250) y el PSG (37,500). El mejor español en esta fotografía es el Barcelona, quinto con 30 puntos. La fotografía general deja una conclusión clara: la Premier mantiene su hegemonía gracias a la profundidad de sus participantes, pero España continúa siendo la principal alternativa. Con ocho clubes aún en liza y una segunda posición firme en el coeficiente de la temporada, LaLiga sigue sosteniendo su peso específico en Europa y alimentando una carrera que, de momento, tiene acento inglés.

articles.title: Harry Kane hopes Ballon d’Or produces ‘special night’ in hometown
articles.summary: Kane, who scored 73 goals last season, is among the favourites for award with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is hoping for a “special night” at Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in his hometown of London, where the England captain is the bookies’ favourite.

The 33-year-old scored 73 goals for club and country last season, the second-best mark in history after Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2010-2011.

But in continuing his habit of tormenting old foes Arsenal on Wednesday, the former Tottenham striker again demonstrated how complete a player he has become since moving to Germany in 2023.

At one point, dropping back to take goal kicks to ignite Bayern’s attack, Kane also set up Alphonso Davies’s first-half equaliser with a pinpoint long-range pass.

In the second half, Kane won and then converted a penalty, giving Bayern the lead before England teammate Declan Rice scored late to grab a share of the spoils for Arsenal with a 2-2 finish.

Kane is odds-on to claim what would be his first Ballon d’Or, but the outcome is anything but certain in one of the most open fields in recent memory.

The Bayern striker faces stiff competition from Spain’s World Cup-winning duo Lamine Yamal and Rodri along with France captain Kylian Mbappe and teammate Michael Olise.

While Yamal and Mbappe in particular have taken to the airways to extol their suitability for the award, Kane has been typically circumspect despite constant media questioning.

Repeatedly asked about his chances after Wednesday’s star showing, Kane said: “I try not to think about it. Obviously, it’s hard.

“There’s rumours flying around, so you try and stay away from it. I’m going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It’s a big occasion and a big event.”

Officially, there are three broad criteria upon which the Ballon d’Or is awarded: individual performances and impressive character, team performances and class/fairplay.

In recent years, recipients have either won the Champions League and/or World Cup or have made their case through sheer weight of numbers. Kane clearly satisfies the latter criteria.

Long criticised for a failure to win team trophies at Tottenham, Kane brought his total to five with Bayern after last year’s league and cup double, but the Bavarian giants’ dominance of Germany may count against him.

Bayern made the semifinals of the Champions League, going out narrowly to eventual champions Paris Saint-Germain.

England finished third at the World Cup with captain Kane scoring six times and laying on an assist.

After scoring against Arsenal, Kane has at least one goal in each of his past 10 Champions League matches, one short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of 11.

“Whenever you’re in any conversation with Ronaldo it means you’re doing something special, especially in this competition,” Kane said.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany praised Kane’s team-focused efforts, saying: “What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here.

“Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he plays for the team.”

After Wednesday’s match, Rice had special praise for his international captain.

“Harry is the clear winner [of the Ballon d’Or]. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he had is remarkable.

“For a striker to play that pass for their first goal, then take the penalty how he did, … he’s ridiculous. He’s such a good player.”

Former Three Lions midfielder Steven Gerrard on Wednesday joined Jude Bellingham in calling Kane “arguably the best England player there’s been” after Kane’s masterclass against Arsenal.

Michael Owen was England’s last Ballon d’Or recipient, winning it in 2001, while in 1981 another striker, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, was the last Bayern player to claim the honour.

“Monday could be a special night. We’ll have to wait and see,” Kane said on Wednesday.

“I’m trying not to think about it too much because we have important games and another one on Sunday.

“I know it’s a massive event. I am looking forward to it for sure. Hopefully, it’ll be a special night.”

articles.title: Van Gaal: "Cualquiera puede jugar la Champions. La UEFA sólo piensa en el dinero, es un mundo corrupto"
articles.standfirst: Louis van Gaal recomienda cambiar el sistema de competición y copiar al hockey sobre hielo
articles.summary: Louis van Gaal recomienda cambiar el sistema de competición y copiar al hockey sobre hielo
articles.body: Louis van Gaal, que recientemente acusó al Manchester City y sus 114 trampas de su "sufrimiento", se encendió contra la Champions League y la UEFA en comentado alegato en el programa de televisión 'Nos'. El técnico neerlandés de 75 años, que entrenó al F.C. Barcelona en dos etapas (1997-2000 y 2002-2003), se mostró muy crítico con el nuevo formato de competición de la Champions League. "Es ridículo que la UEFA proponga un formato de competición así. Hoy en día, cualquiera puede participar. La UEFA sólo piensa en ganar dinero. Es un mundo corrupto", denunció furioso para criticar el paso de 32 a 36 equipos y la desaparición de la fase de grupos para apostar por un sistema de liguillas. Su sugerencia sería que existiera una clasificación basada en el nivel de rendimiento, "igual que en el hockey sobre hielo. Hay una A-League, una B-League, etc. Claro que también están la Europa League y la Conference League, pero la UEFA se escuda en eso". Vn Gaal argumentó que "se llama Liga de Campeones, ¿no? Los mejores equipos tienen que jugar. Así hay menos diferencias de nivel y, por lo tanto, menos goles, pero los partidos son de mayor nivel y se ve un fútbol mucho mejor". "Hay demasiados partidos, lo que se debe en parte a la nueva fase de grupos, más amplia, de la Champions League. Como consecuencia, también hay más lesiones", destacó. Louis van Gaal le recomienda a la UEFA, a la que acusa de esconderse, que se centre en la calidad antes que en la cantidad: "Esto da lugar a partidos de mayor nivel y más emocionantes. Y hay menos lesiones. Se lo dije a la UEFA hace veinte años, pero no me hacen caso".

articles.title: Chelsea: The new Victor Moses? How Xabi Alonso has transformed Pedro Neto
articles.summary: Those following Chelsea closely may feel history is repeating itself as Pedro Neto excels at wing-back, much like Victor Moses did a decade ago.
articles.body:
Just as they did 10 years ago, Chelsea are thriving after moving a winger into a wing-back role, with Pedro Neto the latest player to benefit.

A decade ago, it was Victor Moses who made the switch, adapting to Antonio Conte's then-innovative system and helping Chelsea to a 13-match winning run en route to the Premier League title in 2017.

Neto scored twice from wing-back in Chelsea 's 2-0 win at Everton 's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday.

However, the situation could have unfolded very differently for the 26-year-old.

Chelsea did not regard the Portuguese as untouchable during the summer, although they had set a lofty asking price of about £100m.

They knew Neto was among the players frustrated at the end of last season after Enzo Maresca, with whom he had a close relationship, left the club on New Year's Day. His managerial successor, Liam Rosenior, lasted less than four months in charge as Chelsea finished 10th.

At the end of last season and throughout the summer, players including Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Reece James and Moises Caicedo signed new contracts after buying into Chelsea 's revised vision of adding experience alongside the talent already assembled.

The appointment of Xabi Alonso also appeared to win players over, although there were questions about whether Neto relished the prospect of playing at wing-back, and uncertainty over his future persisted until the transfer window closed.

Yet last month, Neto signed a new contract until 2032 after emerging as a key player under Alonso.

Like several team-mates, he has since publicly backed Chelsea 's project under Alonso.

Chelsea are getting the best of both worlds

Perhaps Alonso saw something in Neto that the player did not initially see in himself.

Despite joining Chelsea from Wolves for £54m in 2024, the attacker had never been particularly prolific, scoring 14 goals and providing 27 assists in 135 appearances for the Midlands club.

His output improved only marginally at Stamford Bridge before Alonso's arrival, with 19 goals and 19 assists in 103 appearances.

Since then, however, he has scored four goals and provided one assist in nine appearances this season, despite three of those coming as a substitute. That is more than double the strike-rate he had achieved previously.

Indeed, Chelsea are now getting the best of both worlds.

Despite operating as a wing-back, he is averaging 5.3 touches in the opposition box per 90 minutes compared with 3.6 last season.

His successful dribbles have risen from 1.6 to 1.8 per 90 minutes, while his dribble success rate has increased from 43.5% to 52.6%. He is also creating more chances, with his average climbing from 1.8 to 2.0 per 90, including an increase in open-play chances created from 1.5 to 1.8.

His defensive responsibilities have also increased significantly, with tackles rising from 0.7 to 2.0 per 90 and possessions won increasing from 2.9 to 3.9, all in the Premier League.

It owes to Neto's athleticism, which he has previously attributed in part to growing up in a family of roller-hockey players, allowing him to impact both ends of the pitch.

In Chelsea 's finest hour under the current American ownership, Neto effectively man-marked Achraf Hakimi as Chelsea beat Paris St-Germain 3-0 in the Club World Cup final in 2025.

On Saturday, Alonso said of Neto's position: "You can call him whatever you want. Winger, wing-back, attacking player, defensive player. He can do many things.

"Today he did well. He is very competitive and whenever he is close to the action he is a threat against any full-back."

It is an asymmetric approach from Alonso, who does not demand the same attacking output from his left-sided wing-back, usually Jorrel Hato or Pep Chavarria. That gives Neto greater licence to drive forward on the opposite flank.

In addition, Alonso will appreciate his status as a dressing room joker among his team-mates.

His former Wolves team-mate Conor Coady was working as a pundit for Sky Sports after Chelsea 's 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds , in which Neto scored, and asked him: "When have you ever been worried about conceding goals?"

Neto replied: "Now I am a wing-back, lad."

The response prompted laughter from both men before Neto added: "In my head, I always have to run back and help my defenders as well."

A decade ago, Moses transformed himself under Conte to great effect. Neto has not had to change quite as much. Instead, his switch from winger to right wing-back under Alonso has amplified the qualities that were already there.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest: Oliver Glasner upbeat before Ipswich game
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest go to Ipswich in the bottom three of the Premier League, but boss Oliver Glasner believes they have deserved more this season.
articles.body:
"It feels unfair but I don't want to be complaining and feeling as victims."

Oliver Glasner's words offer a positive outlook as he believes Nottingham Forest deserve more following their disappointing start to the season.

They visit Ipswich Town on Friday following three straight defeats during an underwhelming opening which has left them in the Premier League's relegation zone.

It was not a position they expected to be in after appointing Glasner in the summer, following his exit from Crystal Palace .

They have been agonisingly close to successful results, wasting golden chances before losing at Palace and nearly hung on for a battling point against champions Arsenal last Sunday.

There is belief that progress is being made, but it needs to translate on the pitch.

There is also confidence internally Forest are still on the right track under Glasner, who has impressed with his methods and personality.

He was brought in to take Forest to the next level after lifting the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League with Palace.

Glasner is impatient to repeat that success, detailing how owner Evangelos Marinakis is the only person he has met with more ambition than him.

The 52-year-old has also said he is not a magician and has already spoken to Marinakis about previous slow starts.

He won just one of his opening six games at Palace after replacing Roy Hodgson in February 2024 and then did not win any of his first eight games in his first full season with the Eagles in 2024-25.

That campaign finished with Palace beating Manchester City in the FA Cup final to end a 119-year wait for a first major trophy.

Glasner has reiterated the need for a strategy and consistency at Forest and it is just over a year since Ange Postecoglou's 39-day reign ended after six defeats and no wins in eight games.

Sean Dyche lasted a little over 100 days and while Vitor Pereira took Forest to the Europa League semi-finals and achieved top-flight survival, he was sacked just two minutes before a termination clause expired in June.

Glasner's consistency is starting to become clear with a preferred line-up crystalising with Neco Williams, Matz Sels, Dan Ndoye, Murillo and James McAtee starting every league game. Morgan Gibbs-White would have done so on Sunday too but for a muscle injury.

Club captain Ryan Yates is yet to play a minute, Ibrahim Sangare has managed just one start - despite signing a new three-year contract in the summer - while Callum Hudson-Odoi has had his playing time limited and Ola Aina has lost his place to new wing-back Daniel Munoz.

Given the results, certainly at home, some will be forgiven for believing they deserve more minutes and the players are aware of the growing expectation and pressure.

"We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas," said defender Murillo following the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal .

"We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

"Now we are building our confidence, I think. We have a very good team, experienced players as well. Now we keep going because we know how tough the Premier League is."

Forest are yet to score in the Premier League at the City Ground this season.

They have netted just eight times in the league at home in 2026 so their struggles in front of their own fans are not new.

They were masked by the Europa League victories against Ferencvaros, Porto and Aston Villa but, in the league, they have won just two of 17 home games since November.

Of those eight goals, four were scored against a weak Burnley side in April and they have now gone eight hours and 26 minutes without netting at home.

Overall this season, Forest have scored five times but have a -6.20 xG, which is the worst in the division.

They have had the third-highest number of shots in the Premier League with 120, only behind Manchester United (138) and free-scoring Brighton (125), but only 25 have been on target.

Against the Gunners, they had 14 shots but only two on target and Liam Delap's miss against Palace, Walter Benitez saving his close-range blast , summed up Forest's lack of cutting edge.

It meant Forest have a conversion rate of just 4.17% - the lowest in the division after Spurs rose to 6.06% following Monday's win over Coventry.

"Every team in the Premier League has the quality to come back into a game to score a goal," said Glasner.

"When you play the champions, you don't have seven, eight or nine moments like we had at Palace. You have two or three or four, and if you don't take it, you have always the chance to lose the game."

That view followed spending £50m on striker Delap this summer, who earned praise from Glasner against Arsenal and was also denied by Ezri Konsa's fine block in injury time.

It is clear the intention is there and the Austrian has no desire to dwell on the past.

"We are the only ones who can change it," he added.

"I told the players this is a tough moment and in tough moments in life there's just one way to go through it, you need your family, you need your your friends and you need to stick together and stay positive

"I'm very convinced that we will do this because I know the players and all the character of the players then we will get these scores, we will get the results."

articles.title: Should Man Utd boss Carrick drop Bruno Fernandes for Bournemouth?
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick must decide whether to leave skipper Bruno Fernandes out of Sunday's crucial Premier League clash with Bournemouth
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is never short of advice around how he should do his job as head coach of Manchester United.

Few of his players divide opinion quite so much as skipper Bruno Fernandes.

So, it stands to reason there are a variety of views around whether Fernandes should be dropped for Sunday's vital Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Former Everton and Rangers striker Duncan Ferguson has no doubts.

"It is a big problem for Michael," he told The Overlap podcast. "Put people in the team you trust. Your captain has thrown you under the bus. If you don't think he is playing for you, get him out. I wouldn't pick him even though he is their best player."

Joe Smith, respected host of Manchester United fan channel Stretford Paddock, is of the same opinion.

"I don't think Fernandes should play on the weekend," he said. "I don't think (Lisandro) Martínez should've played against Leeds, because otherwise they're running the ship here."

United fans heading back on flights from Como to Manchester had a view, although much of it was wrapped up in their general thoughts about the club, most of which were negative.

But only one man's opinion really counts. Carrick is the man who picks the team.

His friend and former team-mate Wayne Rooney has a view on that.

"When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart," he said on the United Stand podcast.

"That was the start. We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players because they don't want to take responsibility.

"I was in that situation [as manager at Plymouth and Birmingham City] and if I was in Carrick's position now, I'd come out fighting. There's no more Mr Nice Guy."

Carrick, speaking at a news conference on Friday, refused to rule out dropping Fernandes for Sunday's game.

Many observers were shocked to discover Fernandes was not going to be disciplined for his post-match outburst following the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. They were also surprised that he would remain as Manchester United skipper, when team-mate Lisandro Martinez was fined for attacking the club hierarchy eight days earlier after the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid.

"It was an assassination," one source who has worked with Fernandes previously, told BBC Sport of Wednesday's comments.

"It was unprofessional. Michael's team are killing him."

The issue is whether Fernandes went too far in attacking Carrick's tactics for the Como game, then saying it was on the coaching team on the sidelines to spot the problem and change it, not the players.

Fernandes is one of the most knowledgeable members of Carrick's squad when it comes to football tactics, and is desperate to succeed. His comments, made on TNT Sports weren't off the cuff, or said in an emotional state after a defeat, as Lisandro Martinez's were.

Yet there is also sympathy for Fernandes from some at Old Trafford given the 32-year-old carried out 10 post-match interviews after the Como debacle, and also because, while hardly offering a defence of Carrick, the words were less inflammatory when they were spoken as they seem in text form.

It is easy to point to Sir Alex Ferguson, the former Manchester United manager who was a strong advocate of managers needing to have control over their players and wonder how he would have reacted to such a situation. Challenges to his authority tended to end with players leaving the club.

However, you only need to listen to Gordon Strachan recounting instances from Ferguson's time in charge at Aberdeen on 'The Good, The Bad and the Football podcast' to accept some of the Scot's more extreme methods would not be acceptable in the current climate.

United's hierarchy are keen to get away from the cycle of sacking managers, having dismissed Ruben Amorim last season and Erik ten Hag in the one before.

However, there is also a basic truth that Carrick desperately needs to end the present run of seven games without a win. If they fail against Bournemouth it would equal the sorry run of Louis van Gaal in 2015-16, which was the worst since a Ferguson-led side had eight draws and a defeat during the 1988-89 season.

So, with Benjamin Sesko, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford all ruled out through injury, can Carrick drop Fernandes even if he wanted to?

The Portuguese's link-up with Youri Tielemans has not flourished as imagined.

And the only goal contributions by last season's PFA player of the year have been a hat-trick and assist in the 5-2 win over Ipswich in August and his strike against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK on 10 September.

But, as Duncan Ferguson said, he is their best player. Carrick has to make the call. He needs to get it right.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Date, time, voting, odds, favourites, all-time winners, BOAT explained - everything you need to know
articles.summary: Nominees, voting critieria, the judges, point scoring system, past winners, last England - Sky Sports has compiled everything you need to know ahead of the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London to mark the award's 70th anniversary
articles.body:
Created in 1956 by two sports writers from France Football, a French magazine, the Ballon d'Or is the award given to the best men's and women's player in world football.

France Football remain the organisers of the award and the voting but the ceremony is co-organised with UEFA, European football's governing body.

Initially, the prize was created to crown the best men's player from Europe. In 1995, this was expanded to include non-Europeans playing on the continent before it became a global award in 2007.

The Women's Ballon d'Or was introduced for the first time in 2018. Ada Hegerberg, who was playing for Lyon at the time, was the inaugural winner.

Where is the ceremony and what time is it?

This year's ceremony marks the 70th anniversary of the Ballon d'Or and is taking place in London to pay tribute to the inaugural winner, England's Stanley Matthews.

The venue is the London Palladium theatre in Soho, with the ceremony beginning at 8pm.

Who are the Ballon d'Or 2026 favourites?

Barcelona and Spain winger Lamine Yamal was odds-on to win this year's men's prize, but Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has now taken his place as the bookies' favourite.

London City Lionesses and Spain star Alexia Putellas is the clear frontrunner for the women's Ballon d'Or with her former Barcelona team-mates Ewa Pajor and Aitana Bonmati, the previous winner, closest behind her with the bookies.

For the full list of nominess, go to the bottom of this page.

Players are judged for their performances over the entirety of last season from August 3 2025 until July 19 2026.

The Ballon d'Or is judged across three key criteria, in descending order of importance:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character;

The Ballon d'Or winners are voted for by "an international jury of specialised journalists", according to the awards' website.

For the men's prize, one journalist is selected to represent every country in the top 100 FIFA rankings, and for the women's award it is one journalist for each nation in the top 50.

This is based on the FIFA rankings in effect at the time, which in this instance is from September 8, 2026.

Each "juror" picks 10 players from the 30-player shortlist in descending order of preference.

The shortlist is chosen by France Football's editorial staff, members of L'Equipe's editorial staff, one juror from the previous edition, and UEFA ambassadors Luis Figo and Fabio Capello for the men's trophy and Nadine Kessler for the women's trophy.

The 10 players named by each voting journalist are awarded 15, 12, 10, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 points respectively.

The Ballon d'Or is awarded to the player with the highest total number of points.

If two players are equal on points, the number of first-place votes is used as a tie-breaker, and this will continue with second-place and third-place and so on if the tie persists.

Any dispute from the vote is settled by the editor-in-chief of France Football.

Paris Saint-Germain and France star Ousmane Dembele is the reigning Ballon d'Or winner. The prize has gone to a different player in each of the last four editions, with Rodri, Lionel Messi and Karim Benzema taking home the golden ball.

However, before that Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo dominated the Ballon d'Or for 13 years save for 2018 when Luka Modric picked up the award.

Messi has won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times with his great rival Ronaldo the closest behind him on five. For 10 consecutive years, between 2008 and 2017, they were the only players to win the award.

France legend Michel Platini (1983, 1984, 1985) is one of three players to win the Ballon d'Or three times along with Dutch duo Johan Cruyff and Marco van Basten.

England's Kevin Keegan, who died earlier this year aged 75, has won the award twice - one of five players to do so with Brazilian Ronaldo, Spain's Alfredo Di Stefano and Germany duo Franz Beckenbauer and Karl-Heinz Rumenigge.

Kane is aiming to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since 2001 and the fifth in history to take home the golden ball.

Four players from England have won the Ballon d'Or: Matthews (1956), Sir Bobby Charlton (1966), Keegan (1978 & 1979) and Michael Owen (2001).

The United Kingdom has had six winners in total, with Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) and Scotland's Denis Law (1964).

Kane and Lamine Yamal have traded places as the bookies' favourites for this year's prize, which suggests the voting will be extremely close.

The closest runner-up under the current voting structure, which has been in place since 2016, was in 2019. Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk finished runner-up to Messi, losing by a seven-point margin.

Messi came out on top of another closely fought battle in 2021, beating then Bayern Munich striker Robert Lewandowski by 33 points. Lewandowski was widely expected to win the award the year prior before it was cancelled because of the coronavirus pandemic.

In 2024, when Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior came second behind then-Man City midfielder Rodri, the difference was 105 points.

This year, fans are being asked to vote for their 'Ballon d'Or Of All Time'. So what is it?

Well, anyone can log-in to the Ballon d'Or website to vote on which past winner they believe was the best.

However, they can only pick from one of the 10 players to have picked up the golden ball on at least two occasions.

Those who pay the €1 fee to cast their vote will earn a chance at tickets to next year's ceremony.

The Ballon d'Or ceremony presents a number of awards beyond simply crowning the best men's and women's player of the season. In fact, there are six other prizes up for grabs:

Men's and Women's Young Talent of the Year - First named the Kopa Trophy, this award celebrates the stand-out players under the age of 21. The voting panel is made up of exclusively former Ballon d'Or winners, who cast a top-three vote (awarding 5,3 and 1 points).

Men's and Women's Goalkeeper of the Year - Formerly known as the Lev Yashin Trophy, in honour of the only goalkeeper to ever win the Ballon d'Or, this prize is given to the best goalkeeper of the year. The voting system is the same as the Ballon d'Or trophies.

Men's and Women's Coach of the Year - Previously named the Johan Cruyff Trophy, in honour of the great Barcelona head coach

Men's and Women's Striker of the Year - Initially named the Gerd Muller Trophy, in tribute to the prolific Germany goalscorer, this prize is given to the player with the most goals in the past season in all competitive matches.

Men's and Women's Club of the Year - This award, according to the Ballon d'Or website, recognises "collective excellence, style of play, results exceeding expectations, and titles secured across the campaign". The jury of journalists vote to decide the winner with number of Ballon d'Or nominees the tie-breaker in the event of a tie.

Socrates Award - Inspired by Brazil legend Socrates, this prize is different from any of the others given out at the Ballon d'Or ceremony. It celebrates "humanitarian work, charity projects, and social solidarity initiatives" off the pitch.

Who is nominated for Women's Ballon d'Or?

articles.title: Ángel Torres responde a Bordalás: "Hay que tener la cara como el cemento"
articles.standfirst: El presidente ha respondido a su entrenador en unas declaraciones a la Cadena SER.
articles.summary: El presidente ha respondido a su entrenador en unas declaraciones a la Cadena SER.
articles.body: Ángel Torres ha respondido a la dura crítica de Bordalás tras la goleada sufrida en Conference League: "Lo que no entiendo es qué hace aquí si está tan a disgusto. Decir que yo le he engañado... Hay que tener la cara como el cemento para decirme eso a mí, después de 30 años, que no lo engañé a él ni a nadie. Yo lo que te digo es que tiene que respetar a los futbolistas igual que los futbolistas le respetan a él. No voy a entrar en una guerra de declaraciones a ver quién", aseguró en declaraciones a la Cadena SER. Pese a todo, Torres descarta tomar medidas drásticas: "No, ninguna. No es ningún drama. Él piensa una cosa y ahora los futbolistas le van a demostrar que está equivocado y punto. Y a trabajar. Lo que hay que hacer es ganar en Bilbao y ya está", explicó. El órdago del presidente a su entrenador es claro: "Él ha firmado porque ha querido. De todas maneras tiene la puerta abierta. Si tan malos somos... ¿Qué le vamos a hacer? Esto es el Getafe", aseguró Ángel Torres dejando abierta la puerta de salida a un entrenador que renovó este mismo verano. Además, el presidente no exime de responsabilidad al técnico: "Cuando un entrenador hace cuatro cambios en el descanso es que se ha equivocado". Lo que más ha molestado al presidente es que Bordalás dijese que se siente "engañado". Desveló que no ha hablado con él y que habrá que preguntarle por qué lo dice. "No tengo nada que hablar. ¿De qué voy a hablar? Estamos en un país libre en el que cada uno dice lo que quiere. ¿Qué quiere que yo le haga?", lamentó. Respecto al nivel de la plantilla, Torres cree que "es una de las mejores plantillas que hemos tenido" y choca directamente con las palabras del entrenador. "He decidido alinear ese once, puesto que tenía que dar descanso a jugadores con riesgo de lesión. Me he visto obligado a sacarles en el descanso, puesto que el ridículo era patente y podía ser mayor. Hemos mejorado algo con jugadores que juegan habitualmente, pero se ha demostrado que la plantilla está descompensada. Ha sido evidente que no nos da, no para tres competiciones, ni siquiera para una", dijo Bordalás tras la derrota ante el Lugano.

articles.title: Tchouaméni: "No hubo pelea con Fede Valverde como se dijo"
articles.standfirst: El francés insiste en que el incidente con el uruguayo fue un episodio habitual de vestuario y lamenta la dimensión que alcanzó por producirse en el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El francés insiste en que el incidente con el uruguayo fue un episodio habitual de vestuario y lamenta la dimensión que alcanzó por producirse en el Real Madrid
articles.body: No es la primera vez que Aurélien Tchouaméni trata de rebajar la controversia surgida tras su encontronazo con Federico Valverde, pero sí una de las más claras. El centrocampista francés aprovechó su participación en el podcast The Bridge para volver a pronunciarse sobre el asunto y restar importancia a un episodio que durante semanas ocupó titulares dentro y fuera del entorno del Real Madrid. "No hubo ninguna pelea como se dijo", aseguró de forma tajante el internacional francés cuando fue preguntado por lo ocurrido. Lejos de alimentar la polémica, Tchouaméni explicó que se trató de una situación habitual dentro de un vestuario de élite. "Hubo cosas que pasaron en un vestuario, como pasa todo el tiempo. Pequeños encontronazos...", comentó. El mediocentro incidió en una idea que ya había deslizado anteriormente: que el verdadero problema no fue el incidente en sí, sino la repercusión que adquirió por haberse producido en el club blanco. "Cuando estás en el Madrid, una cosa pequeña se convierte en algo enorme. Todo toma una dimensión mediática increíble", explicó. Según su versión, lo que internamente fue un episodio más dentro de la convivencia diaria de un grupo competitivo acabó convirtiéndose en una historia de alcance internacional. Tchouaméni también quiso dejar claro que la relación con Valverde está completamente normalizada. "Hoy entras al vestuario, estás con Fede, estamos tranquilos, no hay ningún problema. En el campo es igual y la vida continúa", afirmó. Las palabras del francés llegan después de que ya hubiera abordado este asunto en ocasiones anteriores, siempre con el mismo mensaje: normalidad absoluta y ausencia de conflicto real entre ambos futbolistas. De hecho, durante la conversación llegó a comparar la dinámica de un vestuario con la de una familia, donde las diferencias puntuales forman parte de la convivencia. "Somos un poco como una familia. A veces tienes pequeñas discusiones o situaciones así, pero después pasan", explicó, mientras le preguntaban los contertulios si se iba a ir de vacaciones con el uruguayo: "No vamos en las mismas fechas", zanjó el galo entre risas.

articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Anthony Gordon is fuelled by Barca's belief and Ballon d'Or dreams ahead of El Clasico
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon has opened up about his Ballon d'Or ambitions and how playing in Spain is evolving his game ahead of the Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou; Follow Barcelona vs Real Madrid with our live blog on Sunday; kick-off 8pm.
articles.body:
This is a glamorous week for Barcelona's Anthony Gordon, whose club-mate Lamine Yamal and international team captain Harry Kane are vying for the big individual prize.

Gordon played the full 90 minutes in Barcelona's Champions League epic against PSG and will likely have a significant role in the Clasico. As for the Ballon d'Or, he is not shy about his ambitions to be in the conversation for that one day, too.

"I've always dreamt of that since a kid," he told the media at the recent England camp. "I've never had a limit on what I can do in life because I understand that the people who are there at some point weren't there.

"I believe anyone can achieve anything they put their mind to - they just need a lot of luck.

"Things like that are about preparation. When preparation meets luck you get that kind of opportunity. So I'm trying to do everything I can to be the best player I can be. Hopefully I get a lot of luck and then we'll see."

His critics might say that dream is fanciful. But Gordon's self-confidence and improvement mindset has taken him to another level this year.

He was a surprise signing by Barcelona in May, given they could have landed his England team-mate Marcus Rashford for £26m after a positive loan spell. But their £69.3m spend signalled their belief in the potential of 23-year-old Gordon.

Buoyed, Gordon went on to have a standout World Cup with England, scoring in the semi-final against Argentina and ousting Rashford as his country's first-choice left winger.

Two assists on his Barca debut in August made him an instant hit with his new club's supporters. There have been four assists in 10 LaLiga games so far, with his first two goals for Barca coming after the last international break - when his three goals in three games for England included a fine breakaway effort against Spain.

The heights of Kane and Lamine Yamal are stratospheric but Gordon sees Barcelona as the ideal place to continue to climb the ladder - and show Premier League viewers there are many more qualities to his game than some assume.

He is already feeling evolution in his game. "Definitely," was his response when asked by Sky Sports if playing alongside the electric talents of team-mates such as Lamine Yamal and Raphinha was having an impact on him.

"I played in a completely different style under Eddie Howe in Newcastle. We played a really intense back-and-forth. It was always quite exciting games, whereas at Barca, the intensity is a lot more slow because we control the ball so much and we've been quite dominant so far.

"I pride myself on having high football IQ and making the right decisions. Sometimes I probably should be more selfish as a player, but it's not really my nature. So I think going to a team like Barcelona has really suited me.

"And it's maybe highlighting strengths that people didn't know that I had or maybe overlooked.

"Because I'm fast and because I press, that's kind of the only thing people ever speak about, but I've actually got a lot more to my game than those two things."

The numbers point to the different role and demands Gordon is now facing in Spain.

With Barca bossing most matches, he is getting on the ball more and having more opportunities to show his threat. His stats for shots, chances created, taking players on and passes are all up. The drop-off in crossing is reflective of Barcelona's different approach to Newcastle.

"He has speed. He can control the ball. He helps us a lot with his dribblings, always being able to create chances," said Barca boss Hansi Flick in summary.

Gordon, along with fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi, is providing a solid option down the left for the German so far. They've allowed Raphinha to go to centre-forward, where he is posting stunning goal figures, while Gordon reckons Lamine Yamal on the other flank is the best winger on the planet right now.

It all adds up to a mouth-watering Barcelona attack - and a big handful for the visiting Real Madrid defenders at the Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.

When the world watches the Clasico this weekend, Gordon will have the chance to show his rising level among the superstars.

Follow Barcelona vs Real Madrid with our live blog on the Sky Sports website and App on Sunday; kick-off 8pm.

articles.title: El 'estreno' de Gordon
articles.standfirst: El inglés no se ha medido jamás contra el Real Madrid en su carrera ni contra Bellingham
articles.summary: El inglés no se ha medido jamás contra el Real Madrid en su carrera ni contra Bellingham
articles.body: Gordon vivirá este domingo una experiencia inédita en su carrera: enfrentarse por primera vez al Real Madrid. El extremo inglés se medirá al conjunto blanco, en el que milita su compatriota Jude Bellingham, en uno de los escenarios más especiales: el Spotify Camp Nou. Un Clásico siempre es una cita de máxima exigencia, pero para el azulgrana tendrá, además, el aliciente de vivir por primera vez un choque contra el bloque blanco. A lo largo de su trayectoria, Gordon se ha enfrentado en la Champions League a grandes clubes del continente. PSG, Milan, Athletic e incluso el propio Barça figuran entre los rivales a los que se ha medido. Sin embargo, el Real Madrid todavía se le resistía. Este domingo tendrá la oportunidad de romper esa barrera en un partido que concentra todas las miradas del mundo del fútbol. Además, llega en un buen momento de forma y cuenta con la confianza de Hansi Flick. El encuentro tendrá también un componente especial por la presencia de Bellingham al otro lado del terreno de juego. Los dos ingleses jamás se han enfrentado a lo largo de su carrera. Han compartido hasta en 19 encuentros defendiendo la camiseta de la selección inglesa, desde la campaña 23-24, pero nunca se han visto cara a cara en un partido. Los dos internacionales con Inglaterra tuvieron un papel muy destacado en el pasado parón internacional y compartieron protagonismo en tres encuentros. Su conexión sobre el césped quedó reflejada en varias acciones ofensivas: contra España, Gordon vio portería con una asistencia de Bellingham, mientras que contra Croacia intercambiaron los papeles. El domingo cada uno defenderá los intereses de su equipo. Gordon llega, además, con continuidad y números que le respaldan. El azulgrana ha disputado todos los encuentros de la temporada, salvo el compromiso conta el Racing de Santander, y acumula dos goles y cinco asistencias. Unas cifras que reflejan su aportación ofensiva y su capacidad para intervenir en el juego del equipo. Ahora, contra el Real Madrid, Gordon tendrá la oportunidad de estrenarse en el Clásico, medirse a uno de los grandes referentes del fútbol europeo y enfrentarse por primera vez con Bellingham, un compañero de selección con el que ya ha demostrado entenderse sobre el terreno de juego. El inglés tiene más que argumentos para disfrutar de lo que espera que sea una noche mágica.

articles.title: Pablo Martínez, baja de última hora para el Málaga
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista sufre una fascitis plantar
articles.summary: El centrocampista sufre una fascitis plantar
articles.body: El Málaga ya está camino de Vitoria. La expedición blanquiazul ha tomado el avión alrededor de las 10:00 horas de este viernes para afrontar esta noche en Mendizorroza la décima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports ante el Alavés. El equipo dirigido por Juanfran Funes afronta el encuentro con la necesidad de sumar, por fin, su primera victoria de la temporada y empezar a tomar aire en la clasificación. Enfrente estará un Alavés que llega después de haber sumado únicamente un punto de los últimos 15 posibles. El conjunto de Quique Sánchez Flores, sin embargo, mantiene una posición cómoda gracias a su buen arranque de campeonato, en el que consiguió tres triunfos y un empate. Los vitorianos cuentan actualmente con 11 puntos y ocupan la zona media de la tabla. Funes afrontará el partido condicionado especialmente por las numerosas ausencias en las bandas. La principal novedad en la convocatoria es Juani, futbolista del Atlético Malagueño que ya ha entrado en alguna citación del primer equipo esta temporada y que tendrá una nueva oportunidad ante el Alavés. El técnico malaguista contará con seis bajas. Lobete y Aarón Ochoa continúan al margen debido a sus respectivos procesos de recuperación, mientras que Diego Murillo todavía tendrá que esperar para regresar a una convocatoria. El central ya se ejercitó parcialmente con el grupo en la sesión del viernes, pero aún no está preparado para competir. A ellos se suman Juan Cruz y Joaquín Muñoz, ambos fuera de combate por sendos problemas musculares. La última ausencia es la de Pablo Martínez. El centrocampista arrastra molestias en la planta del pie que le han impedido completar con normalidad varios entrenamientos durante la semana y finalmente no estará disponible en Mendizorroza. La otra novedad en la lista es Berrocal, que vuelve a estar a disposición de Funes para un encuentro en el que el Málaga busca dar un paso al frente y romper de una vez por todas su sequía de victorias. articles.title: Etta Eyong: La "piña" del retorno
articles.standfirst: El delantero camerunés recibió el cariño de todos sus compañeros tras conseguir el gol definitivo ante el Athletic Club
articles.summary: El delantero camerunés recibió el cariño de todos sus compañeros tras conseguir el gol definitivo ante el Athletic Club
articles.body: Los goles en el Ciutat de Valencia, sobre todo los que sirven para confirmar un triunfo, se celebran de manera especial. Pero sin lugar a dudas, el tercer tanto del Levante ante el Athletic Club de este miércoles, aún más. Y ya no solo por lo que supuso a nivel deportivo, si no por quién lo protagonizó. Etta Eyong volvió a los terrenos de juego, después de mes y medio apartado por una lesión el recto anterior, y regresó por la puerta grande. El delantero camerunés anotó en los últimos minutos del choque aplazado por la Dana que azotó la capital del Turia en septiembre y que significó el segundo triunfo de la temporada. Un gol que sirve mucho a nivel clasificatorio para los de Luís Castro, pero mucho más a nivel anímico para el jugador. Tras el gol, Etta recibió el cariño de todos sus compañeros, incluso de todo el cuerpo técnico, formando una piña que quedará para el recuerdo del africano y también del aficionado granota. Una escena que demuestra la voluntad firme de seguir defiendo los colores del equipo del barrio de Orriols, al menos, una temporada más. Y sus compañeros lo demostraron con esa escena. Según informó MARCA este pasado mercado de verano, el delantero tuvo la oportunidad de salir traspasado, pero se negó debido a su decisión contundente de demostrar su valía para ganarse la titularidad del equipo. Etta Eyong, que llegó al club valenciano el pasado mes de septiembre de 2025 procedente del Villarreal por una cantidad cercana a los 4 millones de euros, fue una de las sensaciones en el inicio de la temporada pasada tras conseguir cuatro goles en apenas cinco jornadas. Sin embargo, la citación con su selección y la marcha a disputar la Copa África cambiaron radicalmente su estado de forma y fue relevado a la suplencia, momento de la irrupción de Carlos Espí.

articles.title: Qatar to host FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026 final as PSG await continental challengers
articles.summary: Qatar will host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, with the tournament culminating in the final on December 16, when defending
articles.body: Qatar will host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, with the tournament culminating in the final on December 16, when defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will take on the FIFA Challenger Cup winners.FIFA has confirmed that the concluding fixtures of the annual club competition will be played on December 9, 12 and 16, bringing together continental champions from across the six confederations in the race for the title. This will be the third consecutive year that Qatar has hosted the final stages, following the 2024 and 2025 editions.The FIFA Derby of the Americas and FIFA Challenger Cup will be staged at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, while Ahmad bin Ali Stadium in Al Rayyan will host the final.PSG, who won the competition in Qatar in December 2025, will enter the final as defending champions after Real Madrid lifted the trophy in the inaugural edition under the current format in 2024.Three decisive matches in QatarThe FIFA Derby of the Americas will open the Qatar leg on Wednesday, December 9, with Toluca FC, the Concacaf Champions Cup winners, facing the winners of the 2026 CONMEBOL Libertadores at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium.The victors will return to the same venue on Saturday, December 12, to meet African champions Mamelodi Sundowns FC in the FIFA Challenger Cup. The winner of that contest will secure a place in the final against PSG on Wednesday, December 16.The competition features five single-leg matches in total, with the opening two fixtures taking place at the home stadiums of participating clubs as determined by FIFA rankings. The final three matches will be played in Qatar, with four trophies available across the tournament.Mamelodi Sundowns advance after defeating Al AhliThe 2026 competition began in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on August 26, when AFC Champions League winners Al Ahli FC defeated OFC Champions League winners Auckland FC 1-0 in the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Play-off.CAF Champions League winners Mamelodi Sundowns then beat Al Ahli FC 2-1 in Pretoria, South Africa, on September 19, winning the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Cup and booking their place in the FIFA Challenger Cup.Sundowns will now await the winner of the Derby of the Americas for a shot at reaching the final.With PSG already assured of a place in the title decider, the three December fixtures in Qatar will determine which clubs from the Americas and Africa progress to challenge the European champions for the 2026 crown.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brighton will enter Premier League title race if they beat Liverpool and Man City, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Merson says Fabian Hurzeler's Seagulls will "one million per cent" be in the title race if they win their next two Premier League games; watch Liverpool vs Brighton live on Sky Sports Premier League on Sunday; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
The Seagulls currently sit third in the table, behind only Man City and Arsenal, and have won each of their last four league games.

Next up is a clash with Liverpool, live on Sky Sports Premier League on Super Sunday .

Brighton have not won at Anfield in their last six visits in all competitions, but they face a Reds side who are yet to record their first league win there this season.

Then they face Man City at the Etihad on October 31 - three days after the same fixture in the Carabao Cup fourth round.

"That is it in a nutshell: we'll see where they are after the next two games," said Merson.

"If they go and win their next two games, I don't care how long has gone in the season, they are one million per cent title contenders. Then it's a different game. Then they are going to places expecting to win.

"Liverpool are not playing really well. They are not setting the world alight at the moment. But it will be headline news if they get beaten by Brighton.

"And Brighton, at the moment, you would probably say are a better team than Liverpool. But it's the big team mentality. The pressure's different.

"If Brighton go and get beaten by those two teams, no one will say a word.

"If they drew both, that would be amazing, but you'd rather win one and lose one. It's funny how people look at it and think the two draws would look better because they haven't lost. You've got to win football matches.

"For me, it's about going out and putting on a show and making sure they give a good account of themselves.

"At the moment, you're looking and thinking they shouldn't get beaten in those two games, the way they are playing.

"I like what Brighton are doing. I think they've been outstanding. I watched them against Arsenal. They close you down, they play at a tempo, they suffocate you. It doesn't matter how good a footballer you are, if you get people's heads down, they can't do anything. It's as simple as that.

"They've got a lot of games coming up, but they're good testers. If I'm Man City and Liverpool, I don't really want to be playing Brighton."

Carra: Hurzeler's Brighton remind me of Klopp's Liverpool

Speaking on Sky Sports News earlier this week, Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher gave Hurzeler's side a glowing endorsement.

"Right now, they are the story of the season. I just love the way they play," he said.

"They remind me a little bit of watching a Jurgen Klopp Liverpool team; really aggressive, really fast, really direct.

"If you're asking me or most football fans to describe how you want your team to play, how you'd like to watch them, I think it's that. It's fast, aggressive, direct football. All-action with quality.

"Klopp's Liverpool team are one of the greatest teams we've seen in the Premier League era and this team right now are posting similar sorts of numbers in terms of goals scored and all those metrics we used to look at with Klopp."

On Monday Night Football, he added: "I think the style of football Brighton play now is better [than what they played under De Zerbi] or certainly something I'd want to watch more.

"The best way to describe the football is aggressive, forward, vertical, intensity.

"It reminds me of the debates we used to have about Klopp and Pep Guardiola. Two very successful managers, great managers, great teams, but I think most people in this country would almost plump for a Jurgen Klopp style of football, and that's what I think we're watching here."

However, he stopped short of agreeing with Merson's suggestion.

"I'm not sure about title contenders, but I do look at them and think they are where they should be. It's not the case they've had a bit of fortune; they thoroughly deserve to be where they [are]," he added.

"It's very early in the season, but watching them play this early, I think they should be disappointed if they don't make the Champions League, especially if it goes down to fifth.

"They've got to be looking to be around fifth or sixth, maybe even better with the way they've started the season.

"There are a lot of question marks about a lot of teams this season: Liverpool being one, Aston Villa another, Man Utd, Tottenham. Teams you would associate with being around the Champions League positions are not at their absolute best, so I think there's a great opportunity for Brighton to get Champions League football."

articles.title: Martin O'Neill challenges Celtic to 'find a way' in Europe - but are they just not good enough?
articles.summary: The 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo was Celtic's third straight loss in the Europa League; they are second bottom of the table and yet to pick up a point; watch Hibernian vs Celtic live on Sky Sports Football on Sunday from 11am
articles.body:
The Hoops are now 35th of 36 teams in the Europa League after a third loss, this time against Celta Vigo. Only Ararat-Armenia are keeping them off the bottom of the table on goal difference.

A 7-1 hammering of Hearts in the Premiership gave some hope that Celtic were on the up. Instead, their European frailties were laid bare once again.

Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half and for a short spell it looked like Celtic could go on and get those elusive first three points.

However, Spain international Javi Rodriguez scored twice in three minutes - a header then an unstoppable drive - to leave the Hoops with no points from nine in the league phase with five fixtures remaining.

O'Neill said: "We conceded a free-kick and I thought a second before that we should have had a foul for us.

"They score from the free-kick and it knocks us a little bit. It gave them a bit of momentum.

"If [Liam] Scales' header goes in to make it 2-0, we get the three points.

"We've lost three matches now, remarkably we're still in with a chance [of progressing].

"We've got to win here and got to win away from home.

"We take the lead in the game, if we get the second goal we win the match and it changes the whole dynamic.

"It didn't happen, that's it - we need to try to find a way to win European games."

Celtic looked all but certain to be playing Champions League this season when they took a 4-0 aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round, only to concede five goals to drop into the Europa League.

O'Neill's side have lost their last four European matches while shipping 14 goals.

Goalscorer Baur admits Celtic are simply struggling at Europa League level at the moment.

"The focus is performing every three days in the league. That's first and then performing in Europa League or international football as well," he said.

"At the moment, maybe we are not capable to win these games. But in two weeks, that's the next one, against Besiktas, home again. Hopefully a good atmosphere. We need the points.

"The first half was absolutely okay, it was an open game.

"Then we scored, then we had 10, 12, 15 minutes where we controlled it and dominated it, and then they scored, and at that moment the momentum switched completely and we were not capable to switch it again.

"We had no control. We made mistakes, they pushed us in our own half, around our box.

"It's not getting easier now but there's still five games ahead. What else should we do then but believe?

"As I said, five games ahead and the chances are there. We need points."

articles.title: El Sevilla necesita cortar la hemorragia defensiva
articles.standfirst: Tras recibir 10 goles en las tres últimas jornadas, los hispalenses firman su peor registro a estas alturas desde la 2013-14
articles.summary: Tras recibir 10 goles en las tres últimas jornadas, los hispalenses firman su peor registro a estas alturas desde la 2013-14
articles.body: El Sevilla quiere recuperar su solidez defensiva el próximo lunes frente a Osasuna en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. Después de una travesía exigente de tres encuentros ante Barcelona, Levante y Real Madrid en los que solo ha podido rascar un punto de nueve posibles, ahora la prioridad pasa por cortar de raíz la sangría de los goles en contra. El equipo de Nervión ha encajado 10 tantos en los tres duelos mencionados, acumulando un total de 16 en lo que lleva de campeonato. En este sentido, es su peor registro desde la temporada 2013-14. El rendimiento atrás del Sevilla en estos últimos tres partidos contrasta con su arranque liguero, ya que en los seis primeros apenas concedió seis goles, dejando incluso su portería a cero en dos jornadas consecutivas. Sin embargo, los de Luis García Plaza han perdido fortaleza con los tres tantos recibidos ante el Barcelona, los tres en el Ciutat de València y los cuatro en el Santiago Bernabéu. Eso sí, precisamente 10 de los 16 goles que le han marcado corren a cargo de los tres grandes del fútbol español, algo que tampoco sorprende teniendo en cuenta los antecedentes de los hispalenses. Lo más llamativo de este bache defensivo es que se ha producido con una zaga del todo reconocible y consolidada: Juan Iglesias, Andrés Castrín, Kike Salas y Gabriel Suazo. De hecho, el lateral chileno es uno de los tres futbolistas de la plantilla que lo ha jugado todo hasta la fecha junto a Odysseas Vlachodimos y Lucien Agoumé, mientras que el lateral diestro únicamente descansó en los minutos finales del choque en el Bernabéu. En el vestuario saben que necesitan elevar prestaciones de cara a un tramo de calendario clave ante rivales como Osasuna, Getafe y Alavés. "Los equipos tienen virtudes e intentamos contrarrestarlas, pero tenemos que mejorar en ser más contundentes cuando el balón esté en zona dubitativa y que la jugada termine lejos. Creo que somos un equipo que no debería encajar esa cantidad de goles", admitió este jueves Suazo, marcando la hoja de ruta para volver a crecer desde la defensa.

articles.title: El Atlético trabaja sin sus tres lesionados para recibir al Deportivo
articles.standfirst: Cuti, Cardoso y Koke, bajas en la última sesión antes de medirse al cuadro gallego
articles.summary: Cuti, Cardoso y Koke, bajas en la última sesión antes de medirse al cuadro gallego
articles.body: Vuelve LaLiga al Metropolitano. Tras el empate en Stuttgart, el Atlético regresa a su estadio para medirse al Deportivo. Los rojiblancos no juegan en casa en un encuentro liguero desde el triunfo en el derbi ante el Madrid. Semanas después vuelve a su feudo y lo harán con las bajas de Cuti Romero, Cardoso y Koke. Los tres lesionados fueron las tres únicas bajas de Simeone para el último entrenamiento. Los rojiblancos trabajaron en el Centro Deportivo de Majadahonda para preparar el duelo de mañana ante el equipo gallego en una sesión marcada por las ausencias de los dos centrocampistas y del central argentino. Tres bajas importantes para Simeone que tendrá que afrontar el duelo sin tres piezas clave. A las ya conocidas bajas del capitán y el Cuti, se unió ayer la de Cardoso. El americano venía siendo un jugador fundamental para el Cholo. Volverá a tener que tirar Simeone de la pareja Hjulmand-Barrios en el medio del campo. Ambos apuntan a titulares frente al Deportivo. En defensa podría formar con Llorente, Pubill, Hancko y Grimaldo. Giuliano y Lookman acompañarían en los costados a los dos mediocentros. Arriba, Baena y Julián apuntan a pareja de ataque. Habrá esperar para ver las sensaciones de Kang-in tras no jugar en Stuttgart por unas molestias. La presencia del coreano podría cambiar el plan de ataque.

articles.title: Arsenal: Edu to advise Northampton Town after Nottingham Forest exit
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest's former global head of football Edu will serve as a senior advisor to the new owners of Northampton Town.
articles.body:
Former Arsenal director of football Edu will serve as a senior advisor to the new owners of League Two club Northampton Town.

The former Brazil midfielder left his role as Nottingham Forest's global head of football in September and has since joined the board of directors at Bulgarian top , external - flight club Levski Sofia. , external

A Brazilian consortium featuring former AC Milan and Chelsea forward Alexandre Pato completed a takeover of Northampton, who are 23rd in League Two, last month.

Speaking at an open forum event, Cobblers co-chairman Joao Xavier said Edu would help the club navigate "sporting questions" on an ad hoc basis.

Levski Sofia are owned by London-based investment firm Gemcorp Capital, who are an investor in Sports Alpha Capital - the group which has become Northampton's majority shareholder.

Asked about Edu's role, Xavier said: "We are very proud to have Alex [Pato] with us and Edu with us too.

"We became friends as he had a role at Nottingham Forest and I asked him to help me learn more about English football.

"Edu is a senior advisor for one of our partners, acting as an advisor for Levski Sofia and also here, helping us navigate the sporting questions here at the club, not day to day, just when we ask him and when we need him.

"The club will never be part of a multi-club ownership - no other club is part of our project."

Edu's position at Forest came under the spotlight after a disagreement with Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked last September - the first of four managers at Forest over the 2025-26 campaign.

He arrived after six years at Arsenal, where he became the club's first sporting director in 2022 having won two Premier League titles and two FA Cups as a midfielder with the Gunners.

He brought Mikel Arteta to Emirates Stadium, who delivered the club's first Premier League title in 22 years last season, and oversaw the majority of the recruitment of that squad.

articles.title: No Portuguese player has ever scored for Real Madrid since Ronaldo in 2018, until Bernardo Silva against Leipzig
articles.summary: Bernardo Silva makes history as the first Portuguese player to score for Real Madrid since Cristiano Ronaldo, netting his debut goal during a Champions League win over RB Leipzig. The milestone highlights a new chapter in Real Madrid's Portuguese legacy as they prepare for El Clásico against Barcelona.
articles.body: Bernardo Silva has finally scored his first goal for Real Madrid, and the milestone carries an unexpected connection to Cristiano Ronaldo’s departure eight years ago. The Portuguese midfielder opened his account during Madrid’s 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig on October 21, becoming the first Portuguese player to score a competitive goal for the club since Ronaldo’s final strike in May 2018.Bernardo Silva makes his mark in Madrid’s Champions League winSilva scored Real Madrid’s opening goal against RB Leipzig in the Champions League league phase, registering his first goal since joining the Spanish club as a free agent in the summer of 2026. Madrid eventually won 4-1, although the scoreline followed a first half in which Leipzig threatened repeatedly and goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made important saves.Madrid improved after the interval, with Arda Güler extending the lead in the 52nd minute and Kylian Mbappé making it 3-0 in the 83rd. Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for Leipzig two minutes later, before former Leipzig defender Yan Diomandé completed the scoring with a spectacular volley in the 87th minute.Speaking to Real Madrid’s media after the match, Silva said he was pleased to have scored and helped secure the victory, while acknowledging that his side had been more convincing after half-time.“I am very happy to have won this game and scored my first goal with this jersey,” he said. “It was a tough match, where I think we were much better in the second half than in the first.”Silva also said Madrid were still working to find the right balance between keeping possession, creating opportunities for their forwards and playing with the intensity expected of the club.Ronaldo’s final Madrid goal came in May 2018Silva’s breakthrough ended a long wait for a Portuguese player to score competitively for Real Madrid, with Ronaldo the last to do so before him. Ronaldo’s final goal for the club came on May 19, 2018, during a 2-2 draw against Villarreal in Madrid’s final La Liga match of that season.The goal was his 450th for Real Madrid, arriving in the 32nd minute through a precise header from a cross delivered by Marcelo, his long-time teammate and close friend. It was Ronaldo’s final goal, but not his last appearance for the club.A week later, on May 26, Ronaldo played in Real Madrid’s 3-1 victory over Liverpool in the Champions League final, helping the team lift the trophy before leaving that summer. He had joined Madrid in 2009 and spent nine seasons there, becoming the club’s leading scorer before moving to Juventus.Silva, meanwhile, arrived in Madrid after seven successful seasons with Manchester City, where he won six Premier League titles and the Champions League. His first Madrid goal now places him in a small piece of the club’s Portuguese history, following the era defined by Ronaldo.Silva says he is ready to help ahead of El ClásicoSilva’s first goal comes as Madrid prepare for a major domestic test against Barcelona. The teams are scheduled to meet in El Clásico on October 25, with the match beginning at 9pm local time, or 1.30am IST on October 26.Madrid have won all three of their Champions League league-phase matches, against Inter Milan, Roma and Leipzig, and sit fourth with nine points. The Barcelona match offers a different challenge, with José Mourinho’s side still seeking to sharpen its tactical balance while bringing together its attacking players.Silva said he would continue working and remain ready whenever Mourinho chose to use him, whether for a brief appearance or the full match.“I keep working. I’m ready to help this club,” he said. “Whether it’s one minute, five, ten, or ninety… I’ll be training well, helping the group, and the day the coach feels he needs me, I’ll be ready.”For Silva, the Leipzig goal was a personal milestone, but the immediate focus has shifted to Barcelona, with Madrid needing the same composure and control in a fixture that could influence the early La Liga title race.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Diego Pablo Simeone atendió a los medios de comunicación antes de que su equipo reciba mañana al Deportivo. El cuadro rojiblanco suma cinco triunfos ligueros seguidos y quieren mantener esa racha para seguir metiendo presión al Barcelona. El técnico argentino analizó la actualidad rojiblanca. Barrios: "Lo que me importa es que los minutos que esté en el campo lo haga bien. Estamos trabajando juntos para encontrar su mejor versión" Clásico: "Estoy pensando en el Deportivo" Giménez: "No lo puedo separar del rival a la persona, al hombre que me ayudó en el vestuario. Es uno de los centrales más importantes que estuvo en el Atlético de Madrid. Desearle lo mejor después del sábado" Bajas: "Saben que necesitamos de todos. Siempre se puede competir. Eso no cambia que tengan un grandísimo equipo" Papel del Atlético en el duelo Madrid-Barça: "Te pido disculpas, pero Deportivo de la Coruña" Importancia del partido: "Antes está el Levante, el Bayern... Nosotros nos tenemos que posicionar en el partido de mañana. El Coruña viene compitiendo muy bien en todos los partidos que ha disputado. Ya nos enfrentamos en Copa la temporada pasada y nos costó mucho" Pubill: "Repetir el segundo tiempo del otro día. Estuvo al nivel que nos tenía acostumbrados.
